newsitem.title: UK: UK Labour party disciplines MPs.
newsitem.headline: UK Labour party disciplines MPs.

text.p: Britain's ruling Labour party, keen to show itself tough on sleaze, barred two of its members of parliament on Wednesday from holding any office in the party.

Labour's National Executive Committee imposed the suspensions on Mohammed Sarwar while allegations he gave money to an election rival are investigated, and on Robert Wareing after he was reported to have failed to declare a business interest.

Sarwar was later suspended from the privileges of membership of the parliamentary party, meaning he will not be allowed to attend its meetings or represent it on parliamentary committees. A similar sanction was imposed on Wareing last week.

Former Conservative prime minister John Major, defeated by Labour in a May 1 general election, was dogged by sleaze in his last years with more than a dozen ministers and aides forced to quit over scandals ranging from sexual affairs to allegations they were paid to ask parliamentary questions.
In most cases Major backed the ministers until the moment they quit, landing him with a reputation as a weak and ineffectual leader at the head of a sleaze-ridden party.

Labour, which swept to power under Tony Blair in a May 1 election, has set out to show it is different, beefing up its disciplinary code so it can act against an MP for anything which contravenes the broad definition of "conduct detrimental to the party".

Both MPs maintain their innocence. Sarwar, being investigated by police over allegations he gave an election rival in his Scottish constituency 5,000 pounds ($8,289) not to campaign hard against him, has insisted he will clear his name.
Wareing, suspended for failing to declare a link with a firm reported to be in Serbia, says he has done nothing wrong.

"I refute categorically any suggestion that I have ever had a relationship with any company in Serbia or the former Yugoslavia, or any wrong doing as has been suggested by the unsigned and anonymous letter...which lies at the root of this whole affair," he said in a statement on Wednesday.
Both would be expected to resign their seats if they were found to have breached the law or parliamentary rules.
